definitions: To start a journey or an activity with a particular aim or purpose.
To arrange or display things in an organised way.
To present or explain ideas, facts, or plans in a clear and detailed way, often in writing.
To begin a task or course of action with a specific intention.
examples: They set out on their adventure early in the morning.
She set out the refreshments on the table.
The report sets out the company's objectives.
He set out to prove his theory.
pastTenses: set out (past simple), set out (present perfect)
